title: Flipping an identified variable
statement: Let $n,m\ge 0$, let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, let $z\in\{0,1\}^n$, and let $\pi:[n]\to[m]$. For every $w\in\{0,1\}^m$ and $j\in[m]$, if $w^j$ denotes $w$ with coordinate $j$ flipped and $F_j=\{i\in[n]:\pi(i)=j\}$, then $g(w^j)=f\bigl((z\oplus(w_{\pi(i)})_{i=1}^n)^{F_j}\bigr)$, where $g(v)=f(z\oplus(v_{\pi(i)})_{i=1}^n)$ and the superscript denotes flipping precisely the indicated coordinates.
replaced:
For $n,m\in\mathbb N$, $f:\{0,1\}^{n}\to\mathbb R$, $z\in\{0,1\}^{n}$, a map $\pi:\{1,\ldots,n\}\to\{1,\ldots,m\}$, $w\in\{0,1\}^{m}$ and $j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$, define $g(v)=f(z\oplus(v_{\pi(i)})_{i=1}^{n})$, where $\oplus$ is coordinatewise addition modulo $2$, and write $x^{A}$ for the vector obtained by flipping precisely the coordinates in $A$; then
\[
g(w^{\{j\}})=f\bigl((z\oplus(w_{\pi(i)})_{i=1}^{n})^{\pi^{-1}(\{j\})}\bigr).
\]
